technique_cue_notes: F1a-f, F2a/c/e/f, F5a/c/d/f, F8a/b carry cue class 'micrograph'; SEM, TEM, STEM and HAADF are all listed as compatible families, so SEM, TEM, STEM:HAADF and STEM:EDS all pass
F2b (SAED) and F7b have empty cue-class lists, so TEM:SAED and MECH:tensile are unchecked
F7a carries cue class 'mechanical', which maps to MECH; MECH:tensile passes
F3, F4 and F6 are whole-figure crops with no OCR at all, so THERMO:CALPHAD, SEM:EDS and ATOM:DFT are unchecked

merged_nodes.merged: 'a new phase, seen as white spots in Fig. 1d' and 'the new phase was identified as a Cr-rich sigma phase with tetragonal structure'
merged_nodes.why: one phase-identity claim stated twice in the F1 and F2 linked text; the panel that actually shows it is F1e (800 C), not F1d

merged_nodes.merged: 'the short heat-treatment time (2 h) was insufficient for the sigma phase to precipitate' and 'the absence ... is attributed to the sluggish kinetics of solid-solid phase transformation' and 'precipitation of the sigma phase is controlled by thermodynamic driving forces and solid-state diffusion'
merged_nodes.why: three sentences stating the same kinetic-control mechanism

merged_nodes.merged: 'heat-treatment at 200 C effectively maintained strength and elongation' with the 200-600 C rise in yield and ultimate strength
merged_nodes.why: both are the same claim about how the properties move with annealing temperature below 800 C; the 200 C point is one point on that curve

merged_nodes.merged: 'a primary FCC phase ... nearly constant in phase fraction (FCC_2)', 'a secondary FCC phase with stability field limited to above approximately 700 C (FCC_1)' and 'a sigma phase present below approximately 850 C'
merged_nodes.why: one equilibrium-phase-diagram claim read off one panel

merged_nodes.merged: a separate node for the Cr map and a separate node for the Cu map
merged_nodes.why: one colocation reading over two maps of the same field; split from the HAADF/BF node (o5) only because the modality differs (spatial_map vs micrograph)
